findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/candidate-spec-routing.ts:474-477,509-514 — bounded search truncation is recorded only as query_results_truncated, but routing still slices and returns candidates with fullScan=false and scanEscalationReason=null. The canonical M6 plan requires escalation instead of guessing when truncation can affect ranking. Current B-8038 candidate artifact demonstrates the defect: query_results_truncated with no escalation, while generic cli/core alphabetical hits occupy the tail of the 8-document budget. Fail closed or produce a structured bounded escalation before this artifact can guide reviewers; add a fixture proving truncated-hit and cutoff-tie paths cannot silently proceed.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in ec8d248d: ranking-affecting truncation and cutoff ties now create structured escalation and full-corpus path enumeration; focused fixtures pass.

findings.desc: Coverage is not release-ready: the recorded CHK-007:happy:0 evidence claims `node scripts/verify-process-fact-contract.mjs` passes, but rerunning the exact focused suite at current HEAD fails with `scope check: packages/main/src/handlers/story-review.ts missing signScopeCheck`. In addition, candidate-spec-routing-smoke.ts reuses one broad smoke across M6A-F while lacking direct fixtures/assertions for several must intents it claims to prove (filesystem enumeration perturbation and symlink escape, irrelevant 5 MB corpus/cutoff flooding, headHash/storyFilesHash/prompt/candidate-content freshness, and forged/wrong-writer/replay evidence). Fix the current contract failure and add focused negative fixtures or narrow the verification claims before TEST.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in ec8d248d: process-fact verifier now passes and direct determinism, symlink, 5 MB noise, truncation, freshness/tamper and full-scan mismatch fixtures were added.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/candidate-spec-routing.ts:397-425 and :432-438 — primary Codex/Claude executions run concurrently and append to attempts in completion order; accepted proposals preserve that race order, while buildQueryGroups consumes proposal terms in insertion order and truncates at the query-group budget. The same inputs and same host proposal bodies can therefore produce different queryGroups, candidate sets, and artifactDigest solely from host latency. This violates deterministic routing and makes signed evidence non-reproducible. Collect results by fixed host order before overlap and routing, and add a latency-order inversion regression test.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in ec8d248d: concurrent host results are collected in canonical Codex then Claude order; latency inversion regression passes.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/candidate-spec-routing.ts:529 and :546-565 — the artifact records storyInputDigest, but candidateReadBindingErrors never accepts or recomputes the current StoryRoutingInput digest and never compares it. Because routing inputs include title, description, checklist promises/relatedDocs, understanding, and risk signals, those PLAN facts can change after candidate_spec_route while materialHash/storyFilesHash remain code-oriented; scope_check_save and reviewer pass can then accept a correctly signed but semantically stale candidate set. Rebuild the current story input in each gate consumer (or persist a separately freshness-bound input artifact) and fail/warn by rollout mode when storyInputDigest differs; add a regression mutating checklist or relatedDocs after routing.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in ec8d248d: gate consumers rebuild current Story routing input and reject storyInputDigest drift; mutation fixtures pass.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/candidate-spec-routing.ts:508-528 — forceFullScanReason only switches from ranked.slice(0,budget) to ranked. Files with no query match are absent from ranked, so a justified full scan can still yield an empty or partial candidateSpecSet instead of the full indexed corpus. The dispatch prompt only lists candidateSpecSet, making the documented tool-driven broad-review fallback incomplete and especially unsafe for zero-candidate ambiguity. In fullScan mode enumerate every corpus entry deterministically (without embedding bodies), and verify the manifest covers that enumeration; add zero-match plus fullScanReason coverage.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in ec8d248d: explicit full scan enumerates the complete corpus including zero-score files and manifest coverage is required.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/candidate-spec-routing.ts:516-535,581-583 — ec8d248d fixes the partial full-scan enumeration, but conflates every ranking truncation/cutoff tie with an immediate full-corpus scan. scanEscalationReason becomes non-null automatically, candidateSpecSet becomes every corpus entry, and candidateReadBindingErrors then requires every entry in filesReadFully. A common high-frequency term therefore restores the exact all-document full-read/token-exhaustion behavior this Story is meant to remove. The M6 contract allows bounded expansion/reviewer-requested tool-driven broad review; ambiguity must fail closed or request a structured escalation first, not silently authorize full scan. Separate requiresEscalation from fullScan, keep the bounded attempted candidates, and only enumerate all corpus paths after an explicit justified broad-scan decision; add a regression proving truncated common terms do not automatically require all corpus documents to be read.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in 802d8088: escalation-required state is separate from explicit fullScan; ambiguity remains <=8 candidates and never auto scans corpus.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/candidate-spec-routing.ts:509-523 only turns query truncation and cutoff ties into scan escalation. It merely records weak_source_class_coverage, discards the primary-host disagreement fact after optionally invoking agy, and has no mechanical trigger for lifecycle/gate/process-fact/global-rename/high-risk inputs or unmatched high-confidence legacy terms. This contradicts the canonical MUST-escalate contract at multi-host-keyword-candidate-spec-routing-execution-plan.md:306-320 and validation cases at :524-536, allowing precisely the sparse/high-risk/host-disagreement cases to remain bounded without a justified broader scan. Carry structured trigger facts into routeCandidateSpecs, derive scanEscalationReason for every required trigger, and add focused fixtures for weak source coverage, host disagreement, high-risk gate changes, and unmatched high-confidence legacy terms.
findings.resolvedReason: Fixed in 802d8088: truncation, tie, weak coverage, host disagreement, high-risk lifecycle/gate/process/global rename and unmatched high-confidence legacy terms produce structured escalation reasons with direct fixtures.

findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/candidate-spec-routing.ts:525-558 and packages/main/src/handlers/story-dispatch.ts:235-246 — 802d8088 correctly separates requiresEscalation from explicit fullScan and keeps truncated candidates bounded, but no consumer enforces or even renders the new escalation state. PLAN/REVIEW dispatch still shows only ambiguitySignals/scanEscalationReason, and candidate_spec_route text output likewise omits requiresEscalation/escalationReasons. Host disagreement, high-risk lifecycle/gate/process-fact routing, or unmatched high-confidence legacy terms can therefore set requiresEscalation=true without appearing in ambiguitySignals, while the reviewer proceeds as if routing were complete. Make required escalation visible and fail closed at the applicable reviewer/gate boundary until an explicit bounded expansion or justified fullScan decision is recorded; add dispatch/handler tests for a non-ambiguity escalation reason.
